android.desc:
PasswdSafe is a port of the Password Safe (http://pwsafe.org) application to Android.  Password files can be synced from cloud services using the companion PasswdSafe Sync app.  YubiKey NEO tokens are supported for two-factor authentication.  File passwords can be saved on devices with a fingerprint scanner and Android 6.0 or higher.


***Please maintain a known-good backup in case bugs exist***

quotes.text: Also my password manager of choice.  There's an Android app as well: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.jefftharris.passwdsafe.
quotes.story_title: LastPass users warned their master passwords are compromised

quotes.text:
I've used my passwordsafe v3 db with

  * password gorilla https://github.com/zdia/gorilla
  * pasaffe https://launchpad.net/pasaffe
  * passwdsafe (android) https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.jefftharris.passwdsafe

I like a password db format which is portable to different manager implementations on different platforms, and think that passwordsafe v3 is probably a bit better than the keepass format.

(EDIT: and I don't care for integrations with browsers or anything else, they're a bad idea...)
quotes.story_title: Even the LastPass Will Be Stolen
